commentary_text:
Brookhaven’s archive begins before the first ball, with Coral Bay choosing to field and three record systems open beneath the commentary box. The television strip is fastest but often anticipates decisions; the venue board follows the umpires’ signals; the scorer’s paper book becomes authoritative once an event signature has been matched. None of the three is treated as complete by itself. The radio log has a fourth role: it preserves who was at which end and when a replay was introduced, but its casual numerical remarks never overrule an umpire card or a signed over sheet. This division of authority matters because the same pictures repeatedly return after play has moved on, often several overs later too.

Sienna Park starts to Elena Cross with Mira Vale at the other end. A pad deflection in the opening over brings a raised arm from square leg, but the camera cuts away before the scorer can see whether the signal is for a leg-bye or merely the completion of the ball. Television places the run beside Elena while the paper entry remains ringed.

Elena then drives through cover and turns several singles. The broadcast does not publish her personal tally. When Aila Rowan takes over, the opener is beaten at 3.6 and the bails come away. The ground partnership ribbon closes the association at eighteen, yet its division among Elena, Mira and extras is still provisional because the ringed opening-over delivery has not been classified.

The stump-camera picture returns twice while Tara Quinn walks in. Both clips carry the same north-end camera code, the same 3.6 timestamp and the same incoming batter marker. The television operator briefly flashes another wicket icon, but the scorer binds the two pictures to Elena’s one dismissal rather than treating the second angle as new play.

A radio analyst later reconstructs Mira’s opening spell at the crease from the running log. Her bat supplied three during the first association, and she faced no scoring delivery after Elena’s dismissal before Tara settled. The analyst does not know how the ringed pad event will be classified and therefore declines to infer Elena’s share.

Tara’s short stay has a different rhythm. She supplies seven, Mira two, and the interval includes two runs outside either bat. At 5.5 Aila finds the edge and Maris Vale holds the catch. The live event header bears the west-end identifier W055, distinguishing it from the earlier broken-stump event E036 despite a later highlights package placing them side by side.

During that highlights package the gallery first shows E036 from behind the arm, then W055 from square of the wicket, then E036 once more. Aila is credited only when a delivery header and an incoming-batter transition agree. The repeated Elena clip has no such transition, while Tara’s catch brings Rowan Hayes to the middle.

The innings audit desk separates the opening association by event signature. Two byes and two west-end wides are already signed inside that interval, while the ringed pad event remains outside all certified classes. On the innings-wide leg-bye register, two later north-end cards, LB22 and LB51, are already valid. The no-ball page has a matching video pair under review. No aggregate is announced.

Mira and Rowan move the score through a compact third association. Rowan’s bat supplies four, Mira’s three, and three are detached from the batters. Nia Brooke wins an lbw against Mira at 7.5. A stale production template labels the delivery with Aila’s name, even though Nia is visible completing her follow-through from the south end.

The ground desk refuses to decide the bowling owner from the lower-third alone. It records the event signature S075, the striker Mira, the pad decision and the incoming captain Nora Finch. Several overs later the end log will identify who delivered S075. Until then, Aila’s television analysis and Nia’s paper analysis remain locally plausible.

Rowan and Nora begin from the third-wicket boundary, whose team state is preserved in the fall clerk’s sealed line rather than read aloud. Rowan’s eventual contribution within this long stand is one more than sixteen. Nora’s working contribution is shown only on an internal monitor, and the interval’s non-batter component is kept by a separate assistant.

A no-ball sequence interrupts the partnership. Television replays the free-hit setup using the same frame twice and its ingestion service creates two worksheet rows. One row has the live event signature; the other lacks a new legal-ball transition. The no-ball clerk postpones any category decision until the over log returns from the umpire liaison.

Nora drives, cuts and runs hard, while Rowan increasingly turns the strike over. The partnership ribbon on television rises, but a one-run discrepancy opens between it and the paper component ledger. The discrepancy could belong either to Nora or to the illegal-delivery class, so neither source can settle the stand by itself.

At 15.3 Celeste Reed beats Rowan and hits the stumps. The television wicket light changes before its team-score line has caught up. The paper book closes the Rowan–Nora interval at this event signature, and Lena Moss enters. The fall clerk records the legal-ball marker separately from Rowan’s ordinal position.

The partnership assistant’s working non-batter entry for Rowan and Nora stands at eleven. Nora’s personal component simultaneously stands at thirty. Those two working entries share the disputed no-ball frame; both cannot survive once its identity is resolved. Rowan’s bat component, recorded much earlier, is not under review.

Lena and Nora run a brisk association. Lena supplies four, Nora six, and four sit outside the bat. Emilia Shaw breaks the stumps as Lena attempts a second. The batting and fall ledgers accept a run out, but an automated bowling graphic places a mark beside Celeste because she delivered the previous wicket-taking ball.

Production asks whether correcting the bowling graphic would also undo Lena’s dismissal. The scorer explains only the rule: a run out changes the team-wicket, batter and partnership ledgers, but gives no wicket to the current bowler. She points to Lena’s event identifier without reading Celeste’s eventual analysis.

The wide clerk closes the first innings class at eighteen. Four no-ball cards already carry distinct legal-transition signatures, while the matching video pair remains quarantined on a separate page. A separate mid-innings umpire card, LB143, has entered the leg-bye register; the clerk still waits for the square-leg signal from the opening passage. The category sheets are intentionally separate, leaving more than one plausible extras aggregate at this stage.

Jade Sinclair faces two balls with neither batter scoring and with no delivery outside the bat. Celeste bowls Jade. During the walk to the middle for Pippa Lane, the gallery repeats Rowan’s broken stumps beneath a generic Reed strikes caption. The batter transition and event code show that the old Rowan clip is not another Celeste delivery.

Pippa supplies six in her stand with Nora, Nora supplies two, and one belongs to neither batter. Nia bowls Pippa at 18.5. Nora’s innings now spans five completed associations, but the disputed component beside Rowan has not been incorporated into any public personal figure.

The archive then receives the delayed square-leg card from the opening over. Its event signature matches the ringed pad deflection rather than Elena’s cover drive. The signal is a leg-bye. This preserves the opening partnership and team ledgers while moving that run from the provisional batter stream into the appropriate extras class.

Because Mira’s share had been fixed on the radio log and Elena’s innings ended at the opening boundary, the scorer can now reconcile Elena across the partnership, batter and event-class ledgers. The relevant components remain in their original, widely separated archive passages, and no commentator gathers them or states the resulting batter figure.

Ivy Stone joins Nora. Ivy’s bat supplies five, Nora’s four, and one is outside the bat before Bella Marsh catches Nora from Celeste at 19.5. A replay of Nora’s earlier boundary appears after the catch, but the shared frame fingerprint and the closed personal ledger prevent that shot from becoming a second scoring event.

The no-ball clerk receives the over log. The worksheet row without a legal-ball transition is the duplicated picture, while the row bearing the live signature remains. The independently signed cards are kept on their earlier page. Of the matching pair, the clerk retains the row bearing the live signature and strikes through its transitionless twin, without returning to the earlier card list or reading a category count or the innings extras aggregate.

The same identity decision propagates to the long partnership. The run represented twice in the video feed belongs outside Nora’s bat. Her Rowan-stand component is therefore the working thirty with that disputed item removed, while the partnership assistant’s working eleven recognizes the same item on the non-batter side. Neither revised component is announced as a final table value.

At the other desk, the end log for S075 returns. It identifies Nia as the bowler of Mira’s lbw, so Aila’s provisional production mark for that event is void. The event itself remains a team wicket. The decision changes bowling ownership without changing the fall boundary or Mira’s batting dismissal.

Ivy and Clara Bell take two from the last ball, one from Ivy’s bat and one outside it. The innings closes after twenty overs. The venue screen gives only a victory-context graphic later in the evening; it never displays the full innings total in scorecard format during this archive segment.

The scorers begin their interval reconciliation. The batter ledger contains Elena’s inferred opening result, Mira’s eight, Tara’s seven, Rowan’s twenty-one, Nora’s distributed result, Lena’s four, Jade’s zero, Pippa’s six and Ivy’s six. Clara contributes none. These entries are checked against the four extras classes and the closed team ledger, but the sum is not spoken.

The delayed opening card is filed by its own event signature rather than merged into a verbal category summary. The no-ball page retains only events backed by legal transitions, while the bye and wide sheets remain in their separate folders. A second scorer confirms that the four classes are non-overlapping and exhaustive, which removes the last locally plausible alternative ledger without reciting any component count.

The bowling clerk reconciles delivered dismissals against the team-wicket book and the run-out rule. Every accepted credit must point to a distinct live delivery signature elsewhere in the archive; repeated stump clips and the false S075 attribution remain only as superseded audit entries. She signs the reconciliation without enumerating any bowler’s completed row.

Coral Bay’s chase begins with Jade bowling to Aila. At 0.4 the stumps are disturbed. One wide with signature CW004 has occurred in the opening association, while neither batter has scored from the bat. The gallery keeps the dismissal picture on screen as Nia arrives, so the incoming-batter marker rather than the visual cut establishes the event boundary.

Nia is lbw on the next legal ball. The delivery bears a new signature despite following immediately after Aila’s dismissal. A replay of Aila’s stumps appears while the review is explained; it retains the earlier timestamp and does not carry another batter transition. Jade’s wicket ledger must distinguish this new pad event from the repeated stump event.

Maris Vale and Emilia Shaw attempt to settle. Emilia supplies one, Maris two, and a leg-bye sits outside the bat before Jade bowls Maris at 3.6. Later, a generic Sinclair strikes caption is placed over the old Aila clip, but the event archive links the captioned footage back to the opening delivery rather than to another live dismissal.

Lara Holt joins Emilia. Each batter supplies one and their interval has no extras. Nora catches Lara from Tara Quinn at 6.2. A live blog briefly carries Jade’s generic caption beside the paragraph, yet the delivery header, bowler’s end and catcher sequence all identify Tara as the wicket owner.

Sienna Park becomes Emilia’s longest partner. Sienna’s bat contributes four. Emilia’s provisional component on television rises to ten, while an interval assistant opens a non-batter line at five. Two distinct wide cards, CW071 and CW083, are already accepted inside the association. Both component feeds may also have inherited another wide image from before the settled stand boundary.

A timeout sends the screen through three images: Sienna defending, Aila’s opening dismissal, and Sienna again. Jade is now at cover, not bowling. The unchanged Aila event signature and the absence of an incoming batter show that the middle image is archival. The chase wicket ledger remains on its live sequence. Away from the replay monitor, the over clerk files live wide cards CW096 and CW111 under Sienna’s batting interval; neither shares the inherited image’s timestamp.

Ivy Stone bowls Sienna at 12.1. This event closes the fifth chase association, but the television ribbon is one run ahead of the paper components. The scorer will not choose between Emilia’s batter feed and the interval extras feed until the boundary carry can be assigned.

Two overs later the over-transition log identifies the carried wide as belonging inside the Sienna association but outside Emilia’s bat. Emilia’s working component is the provisional ten without that item; the assistant’s non-batter line is the provisional five without an inherited duplicate of the same event. Sienna’s four remains untouched.

Faye Turner then faces two balls. Neither Faye nor Emilia scores and no extra occurs before Ivy bowls Faye. A replay of Sienna’s dismissal fills the walk-in interval, but Faye’s incoming and outgoing markers make clear that live play has advanced beyond the archival picture.

Bella Marsh also contributes nothing, as does Emilia in that short stand. One wide occurs before Ivy bowls Bella at 12.6. The repeated Sienna celebration is shown again between deliveries. It retains Sienna’s identifier, while Bella’s wicket carries a different event signature and a new incoming batter.

Only after Bella leaves does the interval clerk align the Sienna boundary provisionally. The component ledger contains Sienna’s four, Emilia’s revised share and the revised non-batter component, but the row remains unsigned until the wide archive completes its event-identity audit. No ribbon presents a final runs value.

Celeste Reed and Emilia share the next passage. Celeste supplies one, Emilia one and one wide occurs before Rowan catches Celeste from Tara at 14.2. The wide is attached only to this association, so it cannot repair or disturb the separately scoped Sienna interval still awaiting its archive signature.

Ruth Elms stays longer. Her bat supplies three before Mira Vale bowls her. The team state at that dismissal is preserved by the fall clerk, while the over sheet carrying the legal-ball marker is temporarily in another room. Priya Cove arrives for the last association.

A working partnership note remains provisional when a replay of Ruth’s first scoring stroke appears afterward. The replay carries the same event fingerprint, but this local page does not contain Emilia’s component or the interval’s extras card. Its status must be settled against remote ledgers before the row becomes authoritative, and the partnership’s table value is never voiced.

A separate chase-extras audit checks the non-batter events by signature without assembling a category list. It confirms that the Ruth interval carries wide card CW164, while the Lara, Faye and final associations contain none. The opening card and the Sienna, Bella and Celeste cards remain where they first appeared. An old wide clip is still present on the television pass as a plausible rival.

The wide clerk compares the dispersed cards with legal-ball transitions. The inherited Sienna image and the old television clip resolve to already logged signatures rather than fresh deliveries; the cards carrying new transitions remain valid. The clerk does not collect their values into a local tally. With that identity settled, the delayed Sienna partnership row receives its signature because its batter and extras scopes now share one boundary event. No wides total, partnership value or extras total is stated.

Priya begins the final association with a boundary whose square-leg angle is replayed immediately. Her full contribution in the stand consists of that boundary and a single, while Emilia supplies one and the interval has no extras. Television initially advances the team ledger for both camera angles.

The scorer matches the two boundary pictures by frame fingerprint, striker, field map and timestamp. The second image is evidence of the first shot, not another delivery. The inflated television state remains visible for several seconds, while the paper roll-forward from Ruth’s dismissal excludes the duplicate.

The over sheet returns and places Ruth’s dismissal at 16.5. The fall clerk independently records Ruth after eight prior wickets. Neither source repeats the score, and neither resolves the eventual last-wicket state alone. A batter-component card returned in the same archive box records Emilia’s work during the Ruth interval as three completed pairs, without reproducing Ruth’s share or the extras event.

At 17.4 Emilia drives Mira and Jade takes the catch. A parser temporarily credits Jade because it follows the catcher name, but the delivery signature belongs to Mira’s spell. The batting dismissal, team wicket and partnership end remain valid while the bowling ownership is repaired.

Priya is not out and no further ball is delivered. The fall clerk marks Emilia as the wicket after Ruth, the over sheet supplies 17.4, and the scorer rolls forward the team state using the genuine boundary only, Priya’s single, Emilia’s single and no extras. The composite state is recoverable without any source printing it whole.

The chase reconciliation uses two independent conservation checks. The batter ledger comprises Emilia’s distributed innings, Maris’s two, Lara’s one, Sienna’s four, Celeste’s one, Ruth’s three and Priya’s five, with four batters on zero. The extras ledger is exhaustive after wide deduplication. The ten dismissal identities also reconcile with the run-out rule and the distinct delivery signatures already dispersed through the chase, but this closing audit does not enumerate any bowler’s allocation. The same audit accepts the Ruth–Emilia component note after matching its replay fingerprint and its two wicket-boundary identifiers.

The archive closes with Meadowridge confirmed as winner and Jade as player of the match. The production team preserves every provisional strip, replay fingerprint and authority decision alongside the final ledgers. A later annotator can therefore reconstruct the requested cells from shared events rather than from a summary sentence.
